title: Myitche Town Massacre Revealed: Dozens of Civilians Found Killed After Month-Long SAC 500-Troop Military Operation — Bodies Burned, Monasteries Destroyed
detail: Residents returning to Myitche (Myit Khe) Town in Sagaing Region on June 6, 2026 discovered dozens of civilian bodies following a month-long junta military operation that used approximately 500 troops. The SAC column had conducted systematic village-burning across Myitche and surrounding communities; homes, monasteries, and civilian infrastructure were found burned and destroyed. Swel Gyi village alone had 13 confirmed bodies recovered, with reports of victims killed attempting to extinguish fires set by junta troops. Across the broader Myitche area, humanitarian organizations cite 20–40+ total civilian deaths, though access restrictions prevent a definitive count. Separately, a suspected timed explosive device detonated at the Sagaing Immigration and Population Department office on June 5, injuring approximately 20 people (3 staff and 17 civilians, including a 2-year-old child; 4 in serious condition). No armed group claimed responsibility for the immigration office bombing. The Myitche massacre follows a series of SAC mass-atrocity operations in Sagaing Region — including the Kanbalu double airstrike (133+ killed, June 3), the Butalin airstrike (10 killed, March 30), and the ongoing Sagaing aerial campaign — representing the junta's systematic use of mass violence against civilian populations in the PDF heartland.

media.caption: Residents returning to Myitche Town, Sagaing find dozens of bodies after month-long 500-troop SAC operation burned homes and monasteries — Swel Gyi village: 13 bodies recovered.

title: Arakan Army Intercepts 1,000-Man SAC Column in Mindon Township, Magway — Resistance Claims 400+ Junta Troops Killed or Surrendered in Four-Day Mountain Battle
detail: The Arakan Army and allied forces reported on June 6, 2026 that they intercepted a junta column of approximately 1,000 troops heading toward Rakhine State through Mindon Township, Magway Region (near the Magway-Rakhine border) between May 30 and June 2, 2026. Over four consecutive days of fighting in mountainous terrain, the resistance scattered the column — claiming 400+ junta troops killed and nearly 100 who surrendered to AA forces. If confirmed, this would represent one of the single highest junta casualty events of 2026 and demonstrates the AA's expanding operational reach beyond Rakhine State into Magway Region. The AA has previously conducted attacks in Padan Township, Yekyi Township (Ayeyarwady), and the Magway-Rakhine border corridor as part of its strategy to interdict SAC supply routes and prevent reinforcements from reaching the remaining Rakhine holdouts. This action is consistent with the AA's June 4 vow to capture Sittwe, Kyaukphyu, and Manaung before 2027 — the Mindon operation would degrade the junta's capacity to reinforce isolated Rakhine garrisons by road. Casualty claims originate from resistance sources and should be treated with caution pending independent verification; actual figures likely differ significantly.
confidenceReason: High casualty claim (400+) from single resistance-aligned source (MoeMaKa CDM); not independently verified by major Western outlets as of June 7

media.caption: AA and allied forces claim 400+ SAC troops killed or surrendered after intercepting 1,000-man junta column heading toward Rakhine in Mindon Township mountain fighting (May 30–June 2).

title: Myanmar FM Tin Maung Swe Meets Wang Yi in Beijing (June 4–6) — China Pledges to Strengthen CMEC, Advance Strategic Cooperation with New SAC Government
detail: Myanmar's Foreign Minister Tin Maung Swe concluded a three-day official visit to China (June 4–6, 2026) — his first since taking office — meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. Wang Yi pledged to strengthen high-level exchanges, deepen strategic cooperation, advance the China-Myanmar Economic Corridor (CMEC), and jointly combat cross-border crimes including online gambling and telecom fraud scam compound operations. China signaled strong diplomatic support for Myanmar's new nominally civilian government (inaugurated April 10, 2026 under Min Aung Hlaing). The visit came amid the Arakan Army's advance within 5 km of Kyaukphyu — site of China's $7.3 billion CITIC deep-sea port project, natural gas pipeline terminal, and special economic zone — making China's diplomatic engagement with the SAC directly tied to its infrastructure security concerns. Wang Yi's visit in April 2026 (Naypyidaw) and now the FM reciprocal visit to Beijing signals China's most intensive diplomatic engagement with Myanmar's junta since the 2021 coup. The meeting follows Min Aung Hlaing's India state visit (May 30–June 3) and represents a pattern of SAC international normalization efforts despite the ongoing multi-front war and documented atrocities.

media.caption: Myanmar FM Tin Maung Swe and Chinese FM Wang Yi meet in Beijing (June 4–6, 2026): China pledges CMEC advance, strategic cooperation, and joint counter-scam efforts under new SAC civilian government.

title: Resistance Forces Fire Four Rockets at Toungoo Air Base and Kaytumadi Hotel — Attack Reportedly Timed to Min Aung Hlaing's Secret Visit to Bago Region
detail: Brave Warriors for Myanmar and Karen National Liberation Army (KNLA) Brigade 2, Battalion 5 fired four 107mm rockets at Toungoo Air Base (Kaytumadi Air Base) and the adjacent Kaytumadi Hotel meeting hall in Toungoo, Bago Region, on June 6, 2026. According to resistance sources, the attack was timed to a secret visit by junta leader Min Aung Hlaing to the Toungoo area — a claim that, if accurate, would represent the closest resistance strike to the SAC leadership since the coup. Toungoo's Kaytumadi Air Base is a significant SAC military facility in central Myanmar that has been used for staging fighter jets in aerial operations against PDF targets in Bago Region and Tanintharyi. The rocket attack follows a pattern of resistance forces targeting key SAC military infrastructure with 107mm rockets, including the May 23, 2026 rocket attack on the Northwest Regional Military Command HQ in Monywa (8 junta personnel killed, 20+ injured), the March 25 Magway Air Base attack (11 rockets), and multiple PDF precision strikes on junta logistics hubs across 2026. Casualties from the Toungoo attack have not been confirmed. The attack was reported in the June 7 MoeMaKa CDM daily news as an event occurring on June 6.
confidenceReason: Single resistance-aligned source (MoeMaKa CDM); attack details and Min Aung Hlaing presence claim unverified by independent sources
